findings.evidence: .github/workflows/test.yml:165-207,254-255,388-430,476-479; .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh:175; .claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh:1234-1267; .claude/scripts/tests/model-roles.test.sh:202-212,3114-3120; .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh:2683-2689. The workflow's own comment block documents both failures.
findings.description: The blocking L1 job claims to provision a strict environment in which every section can run, but the change set leaves it deterministically red for two independent reasons. (a) With pinned bd 1.1.2 and dolt 2.3.5, workflow-doctor META 8 observes the live pair 1.1.2:53 against DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA_PIN="1.3.0:66", so its control assertion fails. (b) A fresh checkout has no gitignored production embedded-Dolt store, so model-roles 11.4 prints a line-initial skip note, and STRICT_SECTIONS=1 converts that note into a tier failure at run-tests.sh:2683. Installing dolt therefore leaves the blocking job unable to go green. NEITHER CAUSE IS INTRODUCED BY THIS CHANGE SET -- both are pre-existing and merely unmasked by provisioning dolt. FIX: reconcile the pinned bd version with DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA_PIN and make the model-roles witness hermetic by constructing its own fixture store; keep STRICT_SECTIONS=1 only once a fresh checkout emits neither failure nor skip. SCOPED OUT of h2zz by explicit operator decision and filed as claude-workflow-plugin-we57 (P1, the schema pin) and claude-workflow-plugin-qwny (P1, the model-roles store).

findings.evidence: Makefile:493-506. `git check-ref-format 'refs/tags/v1;printf-PWNED'` returned 0. `make -n verify-release RELEASE_TAG='v1;printf PWNED'` printed `bash .claude/scripts/verify-release-manifest.sh v1;printf PWNED` -- two commands, not one argument. Both reproduced independently by the orchestrator.
findings.description: The make variable is interpolated unquoted into recipe shell source. Git permits tag names containing shell metacharacters, so a valid RELEASE_TAG value splits the recipe into additional commands. This is the SAME injection class R5-F5 fixed in release-verify.yml: the CI half was fixed and the local half of the same two-context design was left open, so the class was declared closed while still live. FIX: never splice the make value into recipe source; pass it as environment data and expand it only as a quoted shell variable, preserving the no-argument case so the script still derives the tag from plugin.json.

findings.evidence: .claude/scripts/tests/green-check.test.sh:726-728,742-777,794-805. The adjacent comment already concedes that ppid does not distinguish one orphan from another, contradicting the safety claim made earlier in the same block.
findings.description: The orphan cleanup claims to identify only this invocation's sleep process. Exact argv plus ppid=1 distinguishes `sleep 6` from `sleep 60`/`sleep 600`, but establishes IDENTITY, not OWNERSHIP: the helper returns every orphaned `sleep 6` on the host and the cleanup kills all of them. With two green-check.test.sh instances at 13.A concurrently, either cleanup can kill both instances' targets, and during 13.A-META the helper returns both PIDs while each assertion expects only its own. An unrelated host orphan matching exactly is also killable. FIX: record the spawned target PID or attach a per-run unique argv token, then revalidate that exact owned process before killing it; do not sweep host-global processes by generic argv.
